title_en: A Vision of India Seen from the Himalayas
translation: Sadguru Jivanji Maharaj, travelling on from Naimisharanya, visited the holy sites of Dantanagar in Aryavrat and then went on to Badri. From Badrinath he reached the peak of Kailash in the Himalayas. On the way, in Aryavrat, there dwelt a people called the Paag. He journeyed among them for four days, and on the fifth day was able to pass beyond them, arriving amid the sava-lakh (a hundred and twenty-five thousand) peaks. There he climbed Mount Kailash and sat leaning against a stone slab. As he turned his mind over the four directions of Bharat (India), he saw that every human being in the world was suffering in the fire of self-interested striving — through various forms of worship, ritual observance, fear, superstition, blind faith, the path of the Vedas, and the like. Troubled at heart, he cried out, "O Maharaj — no one truly goes [to You]!" — that is, "O God, in this world, who is it that truly performs loving devotion toward You...
